title: The Complexity of Weak Partition Connectivity in Hedgegraphs
summary: We prove that deciding whether the weak partition connectivity (WPC) of an unweighted hedgegraph is at most a given integer is NP-complete, resolving an open question about its computational complexity. Hardness holds even for connected full-support split systems, where each hedge consists of two nonempty, vertex-disjoint hyperedges covering all vertices. We also obtain hardness on connected edge-colored simple graphs in which each color class is a spanning forest with exactly two nontrivial trees.
